rows.description: A preschooler chooses a seat next to a favourite playmate or a trusted teacher. Sitting close shows liking and comfort, while shifting away may show a quarrel; kids also change seats just for fun, so patterns matter more than one moment.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: playfulness, trust

rows.description: A young child gives a low, pleased chortle when a game, a joke or a surprise works. It signals enjoyment and shared fun; children copy the laughter styles of adults around them.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, amusement, playfulness, surprise

rows.description: A preschooler bursts into giggles during silly play, funny words or bathroom jokes. It shows joy and belonging and spreads quickly; a child sometimes laughs in a serious moment because of nerves rather than disrespect.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, amusement, playfulness, admiration

rows.description: A child bites a lip, covers the mouth or looks down to hold back a giggle in a quiet moment. It shows awareness of rules and effort at self-control; a brief movement break or a whisper later helps release it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement

rows.description: A preschooler wails during a tantrum, then cries while explaining what went wrong. Strong feeling can outrun words at this age; staying calm, naming the emotion and setting a kind limit works better than punishing tears.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: sadness, calm

rows.subtype: Learning it is okay to cry [Regulating]
rows.description: A child who is told stop crying or be brave may learn to hide feelings, while one who hears it is okay to cry learns to handle sadness. Comfort followed by a talk about what happened builds emotional skills.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: sadness

rows.description: A preschooler cheers at a win, squeals at a surprise or whoops on a swing. It signals joy and excitement and is welcome in play, but reading the setting, for example a quiet hospital, is a skill still being learned.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, excitement, surprise

rows.description: A child learns to swap a yell for an indoor voice when reminded, and to scream only for fun or danger. Clear rules, praise for trying and a shared signal help self-control grow gradually.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: playfulness, anger

rows.description: A child gasps at a surprise, a magic trick or a fright. A gasp shows a quick intake of attention rather than a specific feeling, and the face and context tell whether it is joy or alarm.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, surprise, awe

rows.description: A preschooler hums or whistles while drawing or playing, showing contentment or focus. Humming can also soothe worry, so a sudden stop may show a change of mood; a child who hums a lot is usually simply happy.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, anxiety, contentment
